:::{#thm-moore-penrose-minimum-norm}
#### The Moore-Penrose inverse gives the least squares solution of smallest norm

Let $\matr{A}$ be $m \times n$ and $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$.
If $\vecf{x}$ is a least squares solution (@def-least-squares) of $\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$, then

$$
\norm{\vecf{x}}^2 = \norm{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}^2 + \norm{\vecf{x} - \matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}^2.
$$

So $\norm{\vecf{x}} \ge \norm{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}$,
with equality only if $\vecf{x} = \matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$.

:::

::: proof

Let $\vecf{d} = \vecf{x} - \matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$.
By @thm-moore-penrose-least-squares, $\matr{A}\vecf{x} = \matr{A}\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$,
so $\matr{A}\vecf{d} = \vecf{0}$.

Let $\vecf{w} = \tp{(\matr{A}^+)}\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$.
Then

$$
\ba
\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}
&= \matr{A}^+\matr{A}\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}
&& \text{(condition 2 of @def-moore-penrose)}
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{A}^+\matr{A})}\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}
&& \text{(condition 4 of @def-moore-penrose)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{(\matr{A}^+)}\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}}\vecf{w}.
&& \text{(definition of } \vecf{w} \text{)}
\ea
$$

Therefore

$$
\ba
\dprod{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}{\vecf{d}}
&= \dprod{\tp{\matr{A}}\vecf{w}}{\vecf{d}}
&& (\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} = \tp{\matr{A}}\vecf{w})
\\
&= \dprod{\vecf{w}}{\matr{A}\vecf{d}}
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= 0.
&& (\matr{A}\vecf{d} = \vecf{0})
\ea
$$

Expanding $\norm{\vecf{x}}^2 = \norm{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b} + \vecf{d}}^2$ then gives

$$
\ba
\norm{\vecf{x}}^2
&= \norm{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}^2 + 2\,\dprod{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}{\vecf{d}} + \norm{\vecf{d}}^2
&& \text{(expanding)}
\\
&= \norm{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}^2 + \norm{\vecf{d}}^2.
&& (\dprod{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}{\vecf{d}} = 0)
\ea
$$

Equality in $\norm{\vecf{x}} \ge \norm{\matr{A}^+\vecf{b}}$ holds only if $\norm{\vecf{d}} = 0$,
that is, $\vecf{x} = \matr{A}^+\vecf{b}$.

:::
